newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Four injured as Nordic bikers' war flares up.
newsitem.headline: Four injured as Nordic bikers' war flares up.

text.p: A big blast outside a Hell's Angels clubhouse in the southern Swedish city of Malmo injured four people on Thursday in the latest escalation of a Nordic bikers' gang war that has claimed six lives in two years.

The powerful explosion in the small hours of Thursday morning caused widespread destruction to buildings within a radius of several hundred metres (yards) of the clubhouse, which itself was badly damaged.
"All the windows, which were boarded up, were blown out. Large sections of the walls are down and tiles were blown off the roof," police spokesman Lars Hakansson said.
Four people -- including a baby -- from nearby apartment blocks were slightly injured by flying glass and debris, but all were released from hospital after treatment for cuts.
Four other men, believed to be members of the bikers' gang, who were sleeping in the clubhouse emerged shocked but unhurt.
Forensic scientists began an examination at first light, but Hakansson said it was too early to determine the size or type of the bomb, or even its exact location.

He said it was also too soon to make a firm link between the blast and mounting violence among bikers' gangs in a bloody two-year Nordic turf war, but other police sources confirmed this was their main theory.
The rival Hell's Angels and Bandidos bike gangs are fighting throughout the Nordic region with guns, bombs, grenades and anti-tank missiles.
Hostilities flared in 1994 when a Hell's Angels member was shot dead in the southern Swedish port ot Helsingborg.
The latest victim was a Danish Bandidos member who was shot in the head near the Norwegian city of Drammen in July.
The Bandidos, a Danish offshoot of the Texas-based bike gang, have begun to threaten Hells Angels' domination of the Nordic bike fraternity over the past two years.
On March 1 Finnish Bandido leader Jarkko Kokko was shot on a Helsinki street. He died of his wounds in hospital.

Nine days later gunmen killed a Danish Bandido leader and wounded two companions in an ambush outside Copenhagen Airport and a Norwegian Bandido was wounded in an almost simultaneous attack as he arrived at Oslo airport.
Politicians across the region have called for a ban on the feuding gangs, but traditionally liberal Nordic laws governing freedom of association have so far ruled out such a move.
